blocks.text: Real Russian sentences that use what the lesson teaches. Type the missing word, or pick it, until it turns green.

These are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. Each blank is the word the sentence really has; the word in brackets is its dictionary form.

exercises.q: Посмотрите ___ (внимательный) на этот носик.
exercises.prompt: Take a closer look at that snout.
exercises.why: «The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "-ее" (sometimes shortened to "-ей") to the stem of the adjective.» — DLI, Lesson 80. Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Она постепенно придвигалась ___ (близкий) к нему.
exercises.prompt: She gradually moved closer to him.
exercises.why: «Certain adjectives have irregular comparatives»: выше, ниже, шире, короче, легче, глубже, дороже, дешевле, лучше, хуже, больше, меньше, старше, моложе … — DLI, Lessons 80–82. Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: I should pay more attention.
exercises.why: «An adjective in the comparative degree may be followed by the object of comparison in the Genitive case, or by a phrase consisting of "чем" plus the object of comparison in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lesson 80. Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
